meta.provenance: Authored from model knowledge (cutoff Jan 2026). Original explanations. Node names/categories are factual data.

commands.name: Number Slider
commands.description: An interactive slider that outputs a number within a set range and step. Wire it into dimensions, counts or rotation angles so you can drag through design variations and watch the model respond live.

commands.name: Integer Slider
commands.description: A slider constrained to whole numbers, ideal for counts — panels in a facade, treads in a stair, items in a range. Use it instead of Number Slider wherever fractional values would break the logic downstream.

commands.name: Number
commands.description: A simple box holding a fixed numeric value. Use it for constants you want visible and labelled on the canvas rather than buried inside a code block.

commands.name: Boolean
commands.description: A true/false toggle used to switch logic branches, flip conditions or gate parts of a graph. Pair it with If to give a script simple on/off behaviour a non-programmer can operate.

commands.name: String
commands.description: A text input box outputting whatever is typed into it. The usual source for parameter names, prefixes and search terms that the rest of the graph consumes.

commands.name: Code Block
commands.description: A freeform node where DesignScript is typed directly — numbers, strings, ranges like 0..10..2, functions and multi-line expressions. Experienced users compress whole clusters of nodes into one tidy code block; double-click empty canvas to create one.

commands.name: File Path
commands.description: Opens a file browser and outputs the chosen file's path as a string. The standard front door for graphs that read Excel, images or text files.

commands.name: Directory Path
commands.description: Outputs the path of a chosen folder, for graphs that batch through many files or need somewhere to write exports. Combine with file-listing logic to process a whole directory of drawings or spreadsheets.

commands.name: File.FromPath
commands.description: Converts a path string into a file object that reading nodes can consume. A small but necessary adaptor between File Path and nodes like File.ReadText.

commands.name: Number Range
commands.description: Generates a list of numbers from a start to an end value at a given step — the graph equivalent of 0..100..5. The seed of most repetitive geometry: point grids, panel setout, level elevations.

commands.name: Number Sequence
commands.description: Generates a list by count rather than end value — start, amount and step. Use it when you know how many items you need, such as one value per panel or per level.

commands.name: Object.IsNull
commands.description: Returns true for null items in a list, which is the first step in cleaning data that came back patchy from Revit or Excel. Feed the result into List.FilterByBoolMask to strip the nulls out.

commands.name: Watch
commands.description: Displays the data flowing through a wire — values, list structure, nesting depth. The single most important debugging habit in Dynamo: watch early, watch often, and list-structure surprises get caught before they multiply.

commands.name: Watch 3D
commands.description: A miniature 3D viewport showing only the geometry wired into it, independent of the main background preview. Useful for isolating one branch of geometry in a busy graph.

commands.name: Watch Image
commands.description: Previews an image object on the canvas, for graphs that read bitmaps — heightmap-driven facades, image-sampled colour studies. Confirms the right picture is loaded before pixel values drive anything.

commands.name: Color.ByARGB
commands.description: Builds a colour from alpha, red, green and blue values. Feed it into display or override nodes to colour-code geometry by analysis results — area, deviation, parameter values.

commands.name: Display.ByGeometryColor
commands.description: Draws geometry in the preview tinted with a supplied colour, without touching Revit. The standard way to build in-canvas heat maps — remap a value to a colour range and see the gradient across your geometry.

commands.name: Python Script
commands.description: Embeds a Python node with access to the full Revit API, for logic that stock nodes cannot express — transactions, element filters, edge cases. The escape hatch when visual programming runs out of road; keep inputs and outputs clearly named.

commands.name: Note
commands.description: Places a free text note on the canvas explaining what a section of the graph does. Graphs are read far more often than written — a few notes turn a private puzzle into a tool colleagues can trust.

commands.name: Group
commands.description: Wraps selected nodes in a coloured, titled container — inputs, processing, outputs — so the graph reads as a storyboard. Consistent grouping and colour conventions are the mark of a shareable script.

commands.name: Freeze
commands.description: Right-click option that suspends a node and everything downstream of it without deleting anything. Freeze the expensive Revit-writing end of a graph while you iterate safely on the logic upstream.

commands.name: Run (Automatic/Manual)
commands.description: Switches the graph between re-executing on every change and running only when you press Run. Use Manual whenever the graph writes to Revit or does heavy geometry — Automatic is for lightweight exploratory work.

commands.name: Data.OpenXMLImportExcel
commands.description: Reads a worksheet from an Excel file into nested lists, one list per row, without needing Excel installed. The start of every spreadsheet-to-Revit workflow: room data sheets, door schedules, setting-out tables.

commands.name: Data.OpenXMLExportExcel
commands.description: Writes nested lists out to an Excel worksheet, starting at a given row and column. Pair with parameter-reading nodes to push live model data — areas, counts, door ironmongery — into spreadsheets others can work with.

commands.name: Data.ParseJSON
commands.description: Converts a JSON string into Dynamo dictionaries and lists. Useful for reading configuration files or data handed over from web services and other tools.

commands.name: File.ReadText
commands.description: Reads a text file into a single string, ready for splitting into lines and fields. The simple route for CSVs and logs when full Excel handling is overkill.

commands.name: Passthrough
commands.description: Passes its first input straight through, but only after its second input has arrived — a way to force execution order. Essential when one Revit operation must finish before another starts, which Dynamo's dataflow cannot otherwise guarantee.

commands.name: FamilyInstance.Room
commands.description: Returns the room each family instance sits in, closing a gap in the native node set. The key to workflows like writing room names onto furniture and equipment parameters for schedules.

commands.name: UI.MultipleInputForm ++
commands.description: Builds a pop-up dialog with text boxes, dropdowns and selectors so end users can run a graph without opening Dynamo. The de facto standard for turning scripts into office tools, especially via Dynamo Player.
